title: Dr Andreas Marnerides cont.

blocks.text: 30 March 2023
Dr Marnerides re Babies A, C, D, I, O & P
DR ANDREAS MARNERIDES (continued)
Examination-in-chief by MR JOHNSON
(continued)
Cross-examination by MR MYERS
Re-examination by MR JOHNSON
Questions from THE JUDGE Further re-examination by MR JOHNSON
Housekeeping
Thursday, 30 March 2023
(In the presence of the jury)
DR ANDREAS MARNERIDES (continued)
Examination-in-chief by MR JOHNSON (continued)
Dr Marnerides, we've been asked that you keep your voice up, if you don't mind. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can we resume by considering the case of [Baby O]'s brother, [Baby P], please. Adopting the same approach that we have taken with the other cases, can I confirm that your original report was dated 25 January 2019?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Thank you. Did you subsequently write shorter reports on 12 July 2020?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: 20 October 2021?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: 22 October 2021?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: And 11 September 2022?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: I'd like to, as we have before, deal with the material that you received. So looking at your report of 25 January 2019,
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: first of all. With your letter of instruction and terms of reference, did you also receive the following: a copy of the witness statement made by Dr Evans on 2 June 2018?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Not with, but a year later.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Right. Very good.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: But I did receive that.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes. In any event, before you did the report?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Thank you. A PDF bundle of 603 pages of medical records relating to [Baby P]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: A radiology report containing the post-mortem skeletal survey radiology report?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Sixteen digital photographs taken at the post-mortem examination?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Five digital photos illustrating the radiological images?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Slides from the post-mortem, pathology slides and paperwork consisting of 68 pages?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Some further pathology paperwork consisting of a further 70 pages?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: And 220 pages from the coroner's records?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Then finally, a total of 20 histology slides made up at the post-mortem or after the post-mortem?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Just going to additional material that you have received and you dealt with in your statement of 20 October 2021. Did you receive Dr Bohin's medical reports?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Let me just find the page.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: It's 20/10/21. I think you may have gone too far.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I received the report by Dr Bohin.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: The report is dated 22 May 2020; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Also, Professor Arthurs' report of 19 May 2020?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Additional reports of Dr Evans, dated November 2017 and March 2019?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: And also a reconstituted bundle of medical records?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Are these all -- is this all material that you have taken into account ultimately in reaching your opinions in this case?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't say ultimately, I need to check if I have listed anything in the subsequent reports --
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- additional.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: I think in your -- well, let's go through it for the sake of completeness. Your final report of 11 September 2022, is that a comprehensive list of documents that you have considered?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: It goes to, I think, 56 separate items.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: It includes all the material that we have referred to earlier, albeit you then break down, I think, on an individual basis some of the photographs and similar material; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: If there's any doubt about it, in total, by the time you concluded your written views in this case -- I'm looking at your items 35 to 38 -- you had seen four separate reports from Dr Bohin, two dated 22 May 2020 and two documents that bore the date 15 October 2021?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: You had two separate reports from Professor Arthurs, which are items 39 and 34?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So far as Dr Evans was concerned, I think you had a total of seven separate documents, seven separate reports?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Six.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Six, sorry. You're quite right. I beg your pardon.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You also had what the jury have already heard referred to from time to time as the joint expert report, which was the product of a meeting to which you made reference yesterday?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Because we have dealt with so many cases over the last 24 hours, in order to just put us all back into a mindset where we remember some of the more important detail of [Baby P]'s short life, I just want to run through the chronology, if I may, which you have set out in your first report on 25 January. This is in the "Response to my instructions" section of that report.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do you record that [Baby P] was born with his brothers on 21 June 2016?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: If Mr Murphy can help with the presentation, that's tile 2. His birth weight was 2,066 grams. You record his Apgar scores, which we can see there reproduced on screen.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Tile 7, Mr Murphy, please. You record next that [Baby P] was admitted to the neonatal unit at 14.45 that same day. His temperature, his heart rate and respiratory rate are all -- and oxygen saturations are recorded in your report. You also note, which is material at tile 7 and that he was born in good condition and he was making good respiratory effort.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You move on in your paragraph 6 to record the fact that at 11.45 on 22 June, [Baby P] was on CPAP, albeit that specific event isn't noted in the sequence of events, but that by 14.00 hours that same day, CPAP was stopped and he was on Optiflow.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You record that at 02.34 hours on 23 June, albeit he was still on Optiflow, [Baby P] was still in air and not requiring any additional oxygen. That there were no concerns for him at 10 o'clock on the morning of 23 June, his antibiotics were stopped.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You move on at your paragraph 11 to note the basic facts of Dr Gibbs' examination of [Baby P] at 18.00 hours on the 23rd, which is tile 134.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The jury will remember this is the examination noted by Dr Cooke but conducted by Dr Gibbs. The blood tests were ordered and an abdominal X-ray was ordered. You note the blood gas record at 20.27 later that evening; that's tile 178.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You move on at your paragraph 14 to record the fact of Dr Ukoh's examination at 09.35 on the morning of 24 June; that's tile 289.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: [Baby P]'s collapse shortly after the ward round and the calling of someone you describe as "the doctor" at 09.50, who we know was [Dr A].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You record at tile 306 the blood gas record shortly afterwards at 09.51.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: At tile 362, your paragraph 16, you record the observations at that stage. It may be I've got the wrong tile number there. I think it's 361, actually.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I beg your pardon. It's [Dr B]'s notes relating to that.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You record the fact of a further desaturation, which we have at tile 414, which happened at 12.28 or thereabouts, which is a desaturation that happened at the time [Dr A] and [Dr B] were in the tea room, according to evidence given by [Dr B]; the reintubation of [Baby P] at that stage and the administration of adrenaline thereafter; the right-sided pneumothorax, which was revealed by a chest X-ray, which was decompressed with the needle at 12.40, which is tile 430; the insertion of the pigtail
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: drain, which is tile 539, 15.00 hours; [Baby P]'s further cardiorespiratory arrest, which started at 15.14 and ended with his death shortly thereafter, which is tiles 546 to 596.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did you move on to consider the findings of Dr Kokai, as contained in his report at the post-mortem examination?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, I did.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: In particular, did you identify injuries to [Baby P]'s liver?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, as recorded by Dr Kokai.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes. So rather than dealing with Dr Kokai's findings and then going to the pictures, which we have, so these are perhaps less traumatic pictures than yesterday, if you could talk us through the pictures, please, as to what it is we can see. So we have the -- before we deal with this, is what we are about to see broadly similar in the sense that we will be looking primarily at [Baby P]'s liver?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We will be looking at [Baby P]'s liver, yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: These are photographs, as we know, that were taken at the time of the post-mortem examination. What I would like to do, please, Dr Marnerides, is go through them one by one and for you to incorporate the findings made at the time, if you would, and explain to us what it is we can see before we move on to other material evidence in your conclusions. So that's photograph 1, which shows nothing at all, really.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Number 2. Is that -- I don't know if Dr Marnerides can control the screen. We'll give you control of the screen, doctor. This is essentially exactly the same picture that we saw in [Baby O]'s case, is it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It is yes. Will the jury need reminding of the anatomy?
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: I hope not. No, the jury's heard an awful lot of medical evidence and they know what to focus on.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We know that the liver is depicted there. You went through the anatomy very clearly yesterday, if I may say so, thank you, doctor.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I think Mr Murphy had better take back control.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (Pause)
Until we get back to control, can I just make some comments?
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think these will help the jury. We've got the findings on the baby's liver. We park that information for the time being. We can go through it now --
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Well, whichever way you think is the most helpful, Dr Marnerides. I'll defer to you on that.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We've got the information from the liver. We'll need to assess the information. I will take you through what I felt was important in that assessment.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Now, looking to the other findings from the pathology, as I explained to you yesterday, when we are dealing with cases like this, we try to see whether we have any findings from the naked eye examination and from the examination of the histology that would assist us in proposing a cause or a mechanism of death. And when we get our findings all together we need to see whether the snapshot we have is accounting for the clinical assessment we are being provided. Because we are not the experts in that part, those are the clinicians, they go through the medical records, they tell us what their thoughts are and they give us the information on how the baby was behaving up to the point the baby died.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So having gone through the histology and the findings of Dr Kokai, I had no morphological evidence, which is no naked eye visible evidence, no naked eye visible -- no microscopically visible evidence to indicate a natural disease that would account for the baby's death. And the list of natural diseases I went through in my mind included basically all those that we discussed yesterday.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Now we have the findings from the liver and we need to work out: are these findings due to a natural disease or not?
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So in your assessment of the presence or absence of any natural disease, does that include an assessment of the results of any tests that may have been conducted and that sort of thing?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can only assess the tests that have been conducted post-mortem --
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- and not all of the tests. Even, for example, if there is a metabolic disease screening test, I will take into account the opinion of the expert on metabolic diseases on the report. I cannot claim expertise in metabolic diseases, I will take their opinion on that report. I cannot pretend to be an expert in explaining the significance of tests that were done during a baby's life, I don't have that expertise.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So this is the liver. We remember, right side of the upper part of the abdomen, below the diaphragm.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Dr Kokai reported that there were three small subcapsular haematomas, so bruises on the anterior edge, front edge, of the right lobe of the liver, and these were described as small in Dr Kokai's report.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: This is a photograph of the undersurface of the liver. I will guide you through that. This is the front (indicating). This is the back (indicating).
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: This is the gallbladder (indicating).
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So I think this is one of the three haematomas, looking at it from the undersurface, on the right lobe.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: And there is a further small haematoma here (indicating) that I have identified from my review of the photographs.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: There are three small haematomas on the posterior aspect, so at the back of the liver as well, and you can see these are small, they're not big.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: You just said "on the posterior aspect". What the text says is --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Sorry, apologies, anterior.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: It says:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Three small haematomas on the superior surface of the right lobe and towards it."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So it's the upper part. And these are the three areas.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So it's the superior. And this is towards the front.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So superior towards the front. On this side (indicating).
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Top towards the front?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, top towards the front.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Looking at the script, I think it says "towards it". Does it mean towards its posterior aspect?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: "Three small haematomas on the superior surface of the right lobe of the liver and towards its posterior aspect"?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I think it's a mistake in the text.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes. That's what it should read.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Should it say posterior or anterior?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: It should say anterior. Sorry. Apologies. A mistake on the text.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So it should say, "Its anterior"?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Just so there's a record of this, what's on the screen, for the sake of the transcript, is what is our page J34941, which should read -- the text should read:
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Three small haematomas on the superior surface of the right lobe of the liver and towards its anterior aspect."
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that right?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So the question I am invited to answer is: why are these haematomas there? You can have haematomas in the liver because there is an underlying natural disease. The nature of that disease could be haemangioma, it could be a cyst, it could be, let's say, disseminated sepsis.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: I couldn't see any evidence of that.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: The other explanation could be the so-called haematomas, subcapsular haematomas that we can see related with prematurity. Those look different, however. They are typically not located on the superior aspect of the chest, as we see here, they're typically located strictly on the anterior. Whether this could be a rare manifestation of a prematurity-related haematoma, I could not refute that. That could be an explanation.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: It would not explain, however, the haematoma we saw on the undersurface of the liver.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So although these three could be a rare manifestation of prematurity-related haematomas, theoretically, it wouldn't explain this haematoma here (indicating), which is on the undersurface.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Pausing there for a second, that part of the liver that we see on which there are two circles -- so we're on J34940 and there's a blue circle.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm talking about the blue circle.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Is that the same area of the liver that was injured in [Baby O]'s case or are we talking --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We're talking about the same area, yes. We're talking about the area between the falciform ligament, which we can see here, and the gallbladder we can see here (indicating).
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Is this the same area or a different area of the liver that had, in effect, the full-thickness haematoma that we saw when a knife was used to dissect?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: In the other case, because there were two sections, one of the sections would have been here (indicating), the sections would have been here.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So we have that coincidence between the two cases?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Coincidences are not part of my expertise. I'm talking about this case now.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's the same area, yes. It's the undersurface, yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: If you're inviting me to say are they in any way different, I can say these are much smaller.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: There's no comparison in relation to the size of the haematomas we see here and the haematomas we saw in the previous case. So putting this case on its own, it's a different case.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes. This is a point, I'm sorry to interrupt you, I made with you yesterday or you confirmed yesterday.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You do not look at these cases side by side, do you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, no, I'm looking at this case.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Exactly.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm looking at this case. So the information that the liver gives me on this case is that I've got three haematomas that could be a rare manifestation of prematurity. I've got a haematoma on the undersurface, which is very small and I cannot explain on anything from the medical side of things and I need to consider alternatives.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So the alternatives would be a form of injury to the liver. I don't have features to tell me that there had been severe impact to this liver because I don't have a huge bruise, I don't have haemorrhage into the liver, I don't have the superficial lacerations related with the bruise, so I cannot say there had been huge impact to this liver.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Could it be some sort of impact, for example, due to cardiopulmonary resuscitation? It could be. So I don't feel I can have a confident answer on whether this would be -- on what the explanations for these are. It could be a combined effect of haematomas of prematurity and cardiopulmonary resuscitation, I cannot refute that. Is this an impact, an inflicted injury? I don't have enough to say that. And that's where we are.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So that's this case viewed in complete isolation from [Baby O]'s case. I'm not going to ask you to express an opinion in the light of [Baby O]'s case because that's the jury's function.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, not mine.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: All right. So that's the liver injury. What about other unusual features that you were able to identify in [Baby P]'s case?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Are we talking about the pathology point of view?
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Starting with pathology and then moving on to what you took into account of what other experts said.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: From the pathology point of view, there was evidence, from the examination of the lungs, of features that would be consistent with the pneumothorax complication that had been described. The assessment I'm invited to make in cases where I see features consistent with pneumothorax are: is this a pneumothorax that happened because there is an underlying disease or is it a pneumothorax that happened as a complication of medical intervention?
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: I couldn't see any morphological, so naked eye, or histological evidence that this could be explained on the basis of an underlying pathology. It happened, if I may use the term with a bit of freedom, contemporaneously to medical intervention, which we know can cause this pneumothorax, and I can feel confident to attribute that to that medical intervention.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Otherwise, there was no morphological evidence, as I said earlier, indicating an acutely occurring natural disease process, so a process that would explain why this baby, being prematurely born, collapsed.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So that's from the -- taking into account the views of the other experts?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Did you draw any conclusions as to what it was that had caused the death of [Baby P]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So the assessment of my part, I had no explanation and I could not see how a natural disease would have resulted to that. My understanding of the clinical assessment was that there was no clinical evidence of a natural disease accounting to this and that prematurity, in the absence of an evident clinical or pathological pathway to explain the death, would not be consistent with a natural cause of death.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So we were looking into unnatural causes and the assessment of the clinicians and thereafter the assessment of the radiologists, but I didn't have the radiology the first time, would indicate that there had been excessive injection/infusion of air into [Baby P]'s stomach and intestines.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So far as the evidence that you saw was concerned, what conclusion did you draw then as to the cause of death?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You mean my final conclusion or the conclusion of the first report?
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: No, having taken all the evidence into account, what is --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think it's important to say that at the last report, where I had the benefit of the discussion with the experts present, both from the prosecution and from the defence, I had the benefit of considering other proposals in terms of how that explanation, how potential explanations could be --
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Sorry to interrupt. Prosecution and defence. You said experts from the prosecution and defence?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So you had the benefit of all the discussions?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, I had the benefit of the discussion, listened to the views, listened to what they proposed as things that should be considered, and I came to the conclusion that there was gastric and intestinal distension following excessive injection/infusion of air via the NGT, NG tube, the nasogastric tube.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So air into the stomach through the nasogastric tube?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: And in that context, from that factual position, is the mechanism of death similar to that which you have already described?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. It's the distension of the stomach, either splinting of the diaphragm, acute splinting of the diaphragm, or the vagal nerve stimulus.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Would you wait there, please? There will be some more questions for you.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Cross-examination by MR MYERS

Mr Myers, before you start, what we will do is have a 15-minute mid-morning break, rather than 10 minutes today, because it's a long potential session until 1 o'clock. So if you would, at a moment that is most convenient, as far as you're concerned, from about 11.30 to 11.45, that splits the morning.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, my Lord. It's also very warm, so it'll give us the chance to cool down if possible.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: For example, if we are being presented with, let's say, a baby that is found dead in their cot and the clinical review is that we have nothing to explain that, they have reviewed the medical records, the baby was in hospital for, let's say, 3 days. And if I did the post-mortem or somebody else did the post-mortem and there is a severe head injury, I will go back to the medical records and say: how could they have missed that, did they not do a CT scan? blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes, it's been conducted by the appropriate expert, yes.

blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I accept his findings.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: His findings, yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I accept his differential diagnosis and then I have to -- it's my duty to go through that proposed differential diagnosis and see whether my review would allow one to take a view, yes, that's the more likely or the less likely and so on.

blocks.text: I just want to ask you next something about air embolism itself. Air embolism, as we know, features in this case in a number of the allegations.

blocks.text: When you prepared the initial reports, you assisted us with a number of papers that contained information relevant to this issue, didn't you?

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: I'm not going to start quoting from all of them, but I'd just like to make a reference to them if necessary. One of the papers was a paper by Bernard Knight, a book on pathology by Bernard Knight.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It's a chapter from that.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: I just have that in mind in the questions I'm asking.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Just to assist us all, an air embolism is, in effect, when it creates the problems, serious problems, fatal problems, is in effect an air lock in the heart, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It will go through the heart as well.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: But it's not necessarily only then it can cause the problems.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Is the principal problem created by an interruption in the circulation because of a blockage in the heart?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes. It's one of the big problems, yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: When that happens, is that usually on what's called the venous side of the heart?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Um...
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Blocking circulation on the right side, where it's going to the lungs?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It depends on the quantity of the air. It could be on both sides.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Do you agree with the suggestion or the description that air must enter on the venous side, to be sucked towards the heart, causing pulmonary air embolism?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If it's injected through the veins. If it's injected through the arteries then it's the other way round.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Right. If it's injected through the veins then, it would go into the pulmonary side of the heart?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, and it can return to the arterial side, because there is arterial flow, and go to the rest of the body.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: If we --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So it pretty much depends on the site of the circulation where the initial insertion of air was and the amount of the air that inserted the circulation.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: If we look at the Sally Kinsey exhibit, which is the one we looked at yesterday, page 6, the exhibit setting out the image of the heart. I'd like to look at that.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So we can all follow what's being referred to by the description, the pulmonary circulation or the pulmonary side of the heart is the side that we see where the chambers are blue?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Is that right, Dr Marnerides?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: It's from that blue side of the heart, the chamber at the bottom, the ventricle at the bottom, that it's pumped up through the pulmonary arteries to the lungs, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: So if air comes in through the venous system into the heart and is in a sufficient quantity to cause a blockage there, that interferes with the ability of blood to be pumped to the lungs and be oxygenated?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's... That would be true if we were discussing adults.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: I'm going to come to the position with children in a moment. But yes. With children, where the -- we can see the blue arrow coming -- the arrow coming from the bottom of the blue, the ventricle, thank you, which is just going up to the pulmonary arteries, in children, particularly babies, there may
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: be the foramen ovale there which allows blood to move across; that's correct?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It's open, yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: That's open. So the pressure means that it may move across into the left side of the heart at that point?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It's actually the difference in pressure. My understanding is that it makes it more likely that it will go on that side.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Then of course that can circulate to other parts of the body?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Sorry, more likely than what?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Than continuing downwards into the -- so if I show you.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: The blood comes back to the heart into the right atrium, which is here (indicating). Okay? So if it has air and there is no -and the foramen ovale is closed, as it is in adults, the air will have to necessarily go this way (indicating), downwards, and then pump to the lungs.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: But in babies, because there is a hole there called the foramen ovale, and it's typically open, it has a flap there (indicating), remember that, my understanding of the difference in pressures, left to right, between these two chambers is that it makes it more likely that instead of going this way (indicating), the air will travel this way (indicating), into the left atrium of the heart, then left ventricle, then to the systematic circulation, so the arteries.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: But I'm not an expert in the physiology, so my quotation on the pressures may be wrong. That's my understanding but I may be wrong on that. It's likely because there's a hole there, it'll move that way.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: When the respiration is interfered with because of air embolism, when, for instance, a baby deteriorates, as it is in this case alleged, that will be because blood is not being oxygenated from the pulmonary circulation, won't it?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: You're asking me a clinical question.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: I'm not being rude. Can you not answer that question?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You're asking a clinical question.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: All right, we're at the limits of where we can get to.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: But of course, if air moves across the heart and into the circulation, it is then moving away from the lungs, isn't it, until it comes all the way back round again?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: The paper that you cited from Knight --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: The chapter.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes, the chapter from Knight describes how air remains in the pulmonary side of the lungs and that can cause a blockage in the pulmonary circulation, doesn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That applies to adults.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: And in adults it's the blockage in the pulmonary circulation which prevents the blood from being oxygenated and which would cause the collapse and potentially prove to be fatal?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If that adult doesn't have an open foramen ovale, which can be the case in adults, and that's how adults get strokes, for example, from deep vein thrombosis.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Can you assist, with a baby, maybe you can't, but with a baby, if the baby isn't receiving oxygen, if the air embolus is acting as a blockage, as an embolus, where that blockage is, where it's affecting the baby?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's again a clinical question.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: You don't know?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I can't answer that.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Okay. In any event, in an adult, it's blocking the pulmonary circulation, which is why the blood doesn't get oxygenated?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If the entry is in a vein.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: In the venous -- in terms of evidence of air embolus, the best evidence of course would be a chest X-ray indicating air embolism in situ, wouldn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You mean post-mortem or before death?
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Let's say before death.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I would suppose so. I'm not a clinician.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: With regard to air in the abdomen, so the other mechanism we've been looking at in this case, so far as the pathology is concerned, Dr Marnerides, pathology cannot tell us how the air came to be there, the pathology alone, can it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It can exclude reasons for air to be there. It can discuss potential reasons for air to be there. For example, decomposition. The anatomy is such that it needs to take into account how the air would have gone there.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: To make it more applicable to what we're discussing here, if we are discussing a case with a distended stomach and distended bowels, in vacuum, no clinical information, and I do a postmortem, I would have said, "There is air, there is distension of the stomach, there is distension of the bowels". I have no evidence of a medical disease accounting for that. There's no infection, there is no stenosis, there is no volvulus, there is no necrotising enterocolitis. There's a big list. It's not there.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: There's no anatomical defect to allow air to be trapped there, so the air must have come in, either through the oesophagus or artefactually in terms of decomposition.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: I can assess the degree of decomposition on the post-mortem and say whether, because we know how air is produced in -- how gaseous production is produced post-mortem, it requires a period of time for the bacteria that live in our body, in our gastrointestinal system, to start eating up the tissues, and in that process they create gases and those gases will cause the distension. That's the thinking process.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes. But precisely what that is --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, no, I can't say.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Pathology can't say that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Unless I have clinical or circumstantial evidence saying, yes, there was somebody pumping air or they were doing something, I can't say.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: That's the point, really. You can discount various other mechanisms, but you can't say precisely how it came to be there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Not strictly on the pathology.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: And nor could you say, in fact, in life, how long it would have taken to accumulate in the way that we see on any given radiograph?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: In life, you ask clinicians, not me.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: Yes. Again, because you've given us opinions on air introduced exogenously, I'm just going over where you fit into that, Dr Marnerides. That's why I'm asking these questions.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Whether or not in fact in a baby, at a given point, the air that's described to you would have splinted the diaphragm, whether it did or it didn't, that's something that you take from the assessment of the clinicians, isn't it? blocks.text: I never in my reports or in my opinions in writing said that the distension splinted the diaphragm or induced the vagal nerve system. blocks.text: That's what I wanted to be clear with, Dr Marnerides.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: When you talk about how the diaphragm can be splinted or the vagus nerve can be stimulated and interfere with the system, those are potential mechanisms in which distension could have that effect?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Those are the known mechanisms.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: From the pathology, you don't assert that the diaphragm was splinted in a particular case, do you, from the pathology?

blocks.text: I cannot, and that -- it's not doable from the pathology.
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES

blocks.text: And the same goes for whether or not there's been any interference with the vagus nerve?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Again, it's not doable from the pathology.

Where we can get to on the pathology and then to see the part played by other experts and their opinions.

blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: So when we do a post-mortem examination of a paediatric case -- let's say, the coroner asks me to give a post-mortem examination. In 99% of the cases, even more, the response will be "Pending further investigation" after I've finished my post-mortem.

And our opinion, as for the cause of death in every Coroner's Court, is we are invited, we are asked. That's what we are expected to do: to reconsider our
blocks.speaker: MARNERIDES
